title: Interviews: open questions, in-depth analysis, long answers

blocks.text: In parallel with B2-07, Egyptian track goes to the interview. In Egypt street interviews (raʾy iš-šāriʿ), the podcasts and programs in which the guest tells his life are a very popular genre, and they are also an excellent listening material: short questions, long answers, very spontaneous Egyptian. In this unit you learn to do an interview in Egyptian (open questions, requests for examples and clarifications, active listening) and to answer in a long and orderly way, to refuse with polite personal question and to follow an authentic interview. Nine weeks, in parallel with B2-07, B2-08 and B2-09.

rows: 12–13 9 weeks (weeks) 184–192), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian partner, interviews and podcasts in Egyptian (Appendix C)
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. ask open questions and in-depth questions in Egyptian (iḥkīli, zayy ēh?, ʾaṣdak ēh?);
2. to listen actively, with typical reactions and rewordings;
3. give a long and tidy answer (awwil ḥāga…, il-ḫulāṣa…);
4. to avoid too much personal demand with grace;
5. follow an authentic interview and summarize the main answers.
Nine-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).

The open questions. iḥkīli and waṣṣafli are pronounced with the accent on the long syllable: iḥKĪli, waṣṢAFli. The tone is warm, descending: it is an invitation, not an order. The reformulation. yaʿni ʾaṣdak Inn...? As a real question, he rises to the end: who rephrase asks for confirmation.

Respect the no. In the Egyptian interview, the jokey insistence is normal among friends, but with a stranger a refusal is accepted immediately: ʿala rāḥtak - as you prefer - ma-fīš muškila No problem.

What to choose. Street interviews on daily themes (transport, prices, holidays, sports), Egyptian conversation podcasts, programs in which a guest tells his/her experience. Duration: 4–6 minutes. See Appendix C. The method for an interview.
1. The questions. He listens and writes down all the questions of the interviewer: open, in-depth, hypothetical?
2. The answers. For each interviewee: position in a sentence, an example he makes, a keyword.
3. The "ma"s. Mark the bass, lākin, miš bi-ẓ-ẓabṭ: where does the answer fade?
4. The synthesis. Resuming in Egyptian (il-muzīʿa saʾalit…, wāḥid ʾāl inn..., wi waḥda tanya ʾālit...) and then in English, with the powers (B2-08).
